sections.h2: Where do I go in Trimble County to deal with a tax bill?
sections.html:
Everything happens in Bedford, and the three offices sit within a few doors of each other along Highway 42. The county's PVA page says the assessor works under KRS 132.450 to put every parcel at fair cash value and to maintain the roll that the taxing districts bill from.

Trimble County tax offices, as listed on the county's own office pages
OfficeAddressPhoneOpen
PVA, values property107 Hwy 42 E, PO Box 131(502) 255-35928:30 to 4:30, shut 12:00 to 12:30
Sheriff, takes payment30 Hwy 42 E(502) 255-71388:00 to 4:30
County Clerk, deeds and late bills30 Hwy 42 E, PO Box 262(502) 255-71748:30 to 4:30

All three keep weekday hours only. The sheriff's page lists tax collection among the office's duties next to patrols, vehicle inspections and court security, so ring ahead when you need a payoff letter for a closing date.

sections.h2: What is Trimble County like for a homeowner who needs to sell?
sections.html:
Trimble is one of the smallest counties in the state, a roughly 152 square mile strip along the Ohio River across from Indiana. It was formed in 1837 and takes its name from Robert Trimble. A central ridge runs north to south, with Little Kentucky River and its creeks draining one side and Spring, Corn and Barebone creeks running to the Ohio on the other. The 2020 census classed all of its people as rural.

Bedford, the seat, grew around the meeting of US 421 and US 42 and was known in the 1800s for Bedford Springs. Milton, at US 421 and KY 36 facing Madison, Indiana, is older and was the bigger town until the middle of the twentieth century, when it absorbed the nearby village of Kingston by act of the General Assembly. Smaller places include Wises Landing, Providence, Monitor and Mount Pleasant. The county jail in Bedford dates from around 1850.

The biggest single employer by landmark is the Trimble County Generating Station, on 2,200 acres beside the river about 50 miles from Louisville. Census figures for the county show how a sale here tends to go:

  • Residents: 8,701 as of July 2025, a gain of 2.7 percent over the 2020 count of 8,474.
  • Homes lived in by their owners: 79.7 percent, with 3,931 housing units in all.
  • Typical home value: $172,000. Typical rent: $863 a month.
  • Monthly owner costs: $1,286 with a mortgage and $420 without one.
  • Households: 3,382, averaging 2.52 people, and 93.6 percent of residents had not moved in the past year.
  • Employer firms: 86 establishments with 846 jobs, while 543 businesses have no employees.

Retail sales per person came to $4,123 in 2022, against $12,649 in Union County and $21,716 in Warren County. Shopping and work both draw people out of the county, which is why a quick sale can matter to an owner who inherits a house and lives somewhere else.

sections.h2: How much of a typical bill goes to the state?
sections.html:
The state's cut for 2025 was set at 10.6 cents on each $100 of assessed value, trimmed from 10.9 cents. Applied to the county's typical $172,000 home, that is $182.32. Everything else on the bill, from the county, the school board and special districts, comes on top, and the PVA or sheriff will quote the full rate for your parcel.

A homeowner with the $49,100 age or disability exemption is billed on $122,900, which brings the state's share to about $130.27. A 2 percent prompt payment discount trims the whole bill, not just the state's slice.

sections.h2: How is the Trimble County bill timed and what happens if it is missed?
sections.html:
Statute KRS 134.015 gives the sheriff a four step calendar, and the same one applies in every Kentucky county.

  • Pay by November 1 and take 2 percent off.
  • Pay from November 2 to the end of December and owe exactly what the bill says.
  • Pay during January and add 5 percent.
  • Pay later and add 10 percent, plus the sheriff's own add on fee.

When April 15 ends, the sheriff hands every open bill to the clerk's office. A lien is recorded against the land and 1 percent interest starts each month, with clerk and county attorney fees on top. The state's example of a $1,000 bill shows it at $1,254.00 on arrival at the clerk, and $1,387.79 for a payer who settles within five business days.

The county attorney then writes to the owner twice, first within 30 days and again with the sale date, and the clerk advertises the list at least 30 days ahead of the sale. A sale comes no sooner than 90 days after the handoff. Because the lien can last 11 years and follows the parcel, a buyer's title agent will refuse to close over it. Ask the Trimble County Clerk for the exact payoff and let closing funds cover it.

sections.h2: What is the route for challenging a Trimble County value?
sections.html:
Call the PVA first, since a talk with that office or a deputy is a condition of any appeal. The roll is posted for 13 days beginning on the first Monday of May, with a newspaper notice. If the talk fails, put your appeal in at the clerk's office before the end of the next working day after those 13 days close.

A board of local property owners decides the case somewhere between 25 and 35 days later. It only considers proof presented with the PVA or a deputy in the room, so bring photos, estimates, insurance papers and sales of similar houses. The board puts any change in writing, you may record the proceedings, and a higher final value triggers a supplemental bill for the gap.

sections.h2: Does a Trimble County owner qualify for the homestead break?
sections.html:
The exemption is for owners who are 65 or older, and for those the state treats as totally disabled under a federal or retirement system program. For assessment years 2025 and 2026 it removes $49,100 from the value. File with the PVA at 107 Hwy 42 E, showing a birth certificate, license or passport for age.

Yearly renewal is the rule for disability claims, with two groups let off: veterans with a service connected disability, and owners declared permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems. About 21.4 percent of county residents are 65 or older, so it matters here more than in Warren County, where the share is 14.2 percent.

sections.h2: What paperwork should I line up before a Trimble County closing?
sections.html:
Tax status and the deed are the two gating items. The deed is recorded in the clerk's office on Highway 42, and Kentucky insists that it name each party with a mailing address, state the full price, include an in care of address for the year's bill, and carry a sworn price certificate. It must also cite how the seller took title.

  • Ask the sheriff for a written statement of what is owed.
  • Ask the clerk whether any delinquent bill has been recorded against the parcel.
  • Tell the PVA about the sale if an exemption was on file.
  • Put the buyer's in care of address in the deed.

An owner holding a house with back taxes, a vacant inherited property or a tenant in poor repair does not have to finish these before selling. A cash sale can close as is, with the payoff coming out of the proceeds.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Trimble County?
faqs.a: The Trimble County Sheriff does. The office is at 30 Hwy 42 E in Bedford and answers at (502) 255-7138 on weekdays from 8:00 to 4:30. The PVA only values property.

faqs.q: When does the Trimble County early payment discount end?
faqs.a: It ends on November 1 of each tax year. After that the face amount is due through December 31, and penalties begin in January.

faqs.q: Where is a Trimble County appeal filed?
faqs.a: It is filed with the county clerk after a conference with the PVA. The deadline is the end of the next working day after the 13 day inspection period closes.

faqs.q: What is the homestead exemption worth in Trimble County?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 off assessed value for 2025 and 2026. Owners 65 or older and totally disabled owners can claim it through the PVA in Bedford.

faqs.q: What becomes of a Trimble County bill unpaid on April 15?
faqs.a: It goes to the county clerk as a certificate of delinquency with a lien recorded on the parcel. Interest of 1 percent a month, clerk fees and attorney fees follow, and the certificate can be sold at the annual sale.
